The Forest does not resemble most other National Forests in that it has numerous fairly large but non-contiguous sections scattered across most of the state of Nevada and a portion of eastern California.

About the Agency
Caring for the Land and Serving People
Established in 1905, the Forest Service, an agency of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, is the nation’s foremost federal forestry organization. The agency is a world leader in forest research, providing leadership in the sustainable management, conservation, use, and stewardship of natural and cultural resources on national forests and grasslands in the United States.
Dedicated Forest Service employees manage the National Forest System, which consists of 154 national forests and 20 national grasslands covering 193 million acres in 43 states, the Virgin Islands, and Puerto Rico. The agency’s renowned fire management organization provides critical expertise in making communities and infrastructure safer. Moreover, the agency helps communities; state, local, and tribal governments; forest industries; and private forest landowners improve conditions in both urban and rural areas. In total, the Forest Service helps to steward about 900 million forested acres in the U.S., including 130 million acres in urban areas, which most Americans now call home.

About the Area
Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest
The Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest offers a setting of classic Western beauty and is known for its many recreational opportunities, scenic vistas, and wild places where visitors can still find solitude. The Forest does not resemble most other National Forests in that it has numerous fairly large but non-contiguous sections scattered across most of the state of Nevada and a portion of eastern California. It is divided into seven uniquely different administrative units. Six of the units are referred to as “ranger districts” and one is a “national recreation area.”
Forest offices are located in Austin, Carson City, Elko, Ely, Las Vegas, Tonopah, Wells, and Winnemucca in Nevada and Bridgeport in California. For addresses, hours, and phone numbers for each visit the offices webpage .
Forest Facts and Figures
Image
Image
Located in central Nevada, the Austin-Tonopah Ranger District is characterized by a linear chain of mountains that stretch north-to-south across central Nevada.
Located in western Nevada and eastern California, the Bridgeport Ranger District is known for its spectacular scenery, which ranges from snow-capped summits to crystalline alpine lakes.
Located in western Nevada and eastern California, the Carson Ranger District boasts a varied and spectacular landscape from scenic snowy alpine peaks to the warmer lower valleys of semi-arid Great Basin Desert.
Located in eastern Nevada, the Ely Ranger District is made up of rugged, mountainous terrain, with some of Nevada’s tallest summits, and has nine wilderness areas that offers a solitude-filled backcountry adventure.
Located in northeastern Nevada, the Mountain City-Ruby Mountains-Jarbidge Ranger District’s terrain is composed of rocky peaks, glacier-formed lakes, steep narrow canyons, and rolling hills.
Located in northern Nevada, the Santa Rosa Ranger District is comprised of rugged granitic rock formations and wide, sweeping basins mountains and plateaus.
Located in southern Nevada, the Spring Mountain National Recreation Area’s rugged mountains with towering cliffs, steep hillsides, and deep narrow canyons are surrounded by a desert landscape.
